pi.summary: PI Controller — Core of the control loop
pi.text:
Controlled variable: grid power (positive = import, negative = export). Manipulated variable: AC output power of the inverter.

P-part: responds immediately to the current deviation (grid − offset).
I-part: accumulates deviations over time, eliminates steady-state error.
Anti-windup: back-calculation — after each control action the integral is corrected to the value that produces the actual (possibly clamped) output. When output is not clamped, this is identical to normal accumulation.
Integral reset: reset to 0 on most zone transitions — except case D (recovery), C (zone-3 safety) and G (AC charge start).
Tolerance decay: −5 %/cycle when error ≤ dead band and |integral| > 10.
Zone 0: integral frozen, no PI call.

Error calculation depends on mode:
• Normal: raw_error = (grid − offset) × error_share
• AC Charge: raw_error = (offset − grid) × error_share (inverted)
Error share: two separate pools — Normal is split only among instances in mode '1', AC Charge only among instances currently charging at the same time. With multiple instances in the relevant pool, proportional to usable capacity (SOC − zone-3 threshold); otherwise always 1.0.
Multi-instance output base (mode-'1' pool): the control action builds on (Σ commanded power of all instances in the pool) × own error share, not on this instance's own last commanded value. Realigns the split to the weighting on every control action instead of letting a one-time imbalance between instances persist.

Self-Adjusting Wait: After each output change the controller waits for the actual inverter output power instead of a fixed pause. Once actual_power reaches the target ±tolerance, the controller continues. The configured wait time acts as a maximum timeout.

Starting values: P = 0.5, I = 0. Increase P gradually until output starts oscillating, then step back. Only introduce I once P-control is stable.

zones.summary: SOC Zone Logic — behaviour based on battery state of charge
zones.text:
Zone 0 (surplus, optional): SOC ≥ export threshold AND PV surplus → output at Hard Limit Z0. Discharge current 2 A. PI integral frozen. Always sits on top of an active Zone-1 cycle; on exit the zone is re-derived from the SOC.

Zone 1 (aggressive): SOC > zone-1 threshold → high discharge current, offset 1. Runs through until SOC ≤ zone-3 threshold — no yo-yo effect.

Zone 2 (conservative): zone-3 < SOC ≤ zone-1 → 0 A discharge current, dynamic output limit (min(Hard Limit Z1, max(0, PV − reserve))), offset 2.

Zone 3 (safety stop): SOC ≤ zone-3 threshold → output 0 W, mode disabled. AC charging remains possible.

surplus.text:
Highest priority — blocks tariff charging, discharge-lock and AC charging while Zone 0 is active.

Normal entry: SOC ≥ SOC threshold AND (PV > consumption reference + PV hysteresis OR (PV = 0 AND output = 0 across two consecutive cycles AND PV > 0 measured again since the last exit)). The two-cycle debounce alone isn't enough at night — after an exit PV stays at 0, and as soon as output briefly drops back to 0 again (e.g. while Zone 1 is ramping up), the same branch would fire immediately again. The additional lock (PV > 0 required) keeps this branch disabled after an exit until the sun genuinely returns — the SOC and consumption exits are unaffected. This lock state survives an HA restart.
Forecast entry: forecast ≥ threshold AND PV > Hard Limit Z0 AND SOC > zone-3 threshold (no export threshold required).

Zone 0 always sits on top of an active Zone-1 cycle: entry activates Zone 1, on exit the zone is re-derived from the SOC (SOC > zone-1 threshold → Zone 1, otherwise Zone 2). The SOC threshold must be above the zone-1 threshold — otherwise regulation pauses with an error message.

Exit: PV ≤ consumption reference − PV hysteresis OR SOC < (threshold − SOC hysteresis).
Consumption reference: single instance = output + grid. Multi-instance = (ΣOutput_all + grid) × error share — keeps the dead band consistent relative to true household consumption.
Exit lock (optional): while the power forecast is ≥ lock factor × Hard Limit Z0 AND SOC > zone-3 threshold, only the PV exit is blocked — short dips (clouds) are ridden out in Zone 0 instead of exiting. Rationale: exiting with a full battery enters a state where the hardware throttles PV down to consumption and the surplus becomes unmeasurable — re-entry is then delayed by minutes. The SOC exit stays unblocked and always ends surplus.
Forecast forcing is active while forecast ≥ threshold AND PV > Hard Limit Z0 AND SOC > zone-3 threshold: as long as all hold, exit is blocked (both SOC and consumption terms excluded — curtailment avoidance). Once PV drops below Hard Limit Z0 (incl. at night: PV = 0), the forecast drops below the threshold or the SOC drops below the zone-3 threshold, forcing ends and the normal exit applies. Zone 3 (safety) ends surplus at any time as well.

Output is set to Hard Limit Z0. Integral frozen (no PI call). Output is set to 0 on exit.

ac.summary: AC Charging — grid charges the battery
ac.text:
Entry (case G): SOC < target AND no surplus active AND no AC/tariff charge active AND mode ≠ '3' AND (grid + Σoutput_discharging) < −hysteresis.
Σoutput_discharging: single-instance = own output. Multi-instance = sum over all instances in discharge mode — prevents a sibling instance's discharge from being read as external grid surplus.
Abort (case H): mode = '3' AND ac_charge_active AND no tariff charge AND (SOC ≥ target OR (grid ≥ offset + hysteresis AND output ≤ 0 W)) — output here is always this instance's own charge power; `≤` instead of exact `= 0` is more robust against Modbus noise.

PI controller runs inverted — positive error → increase charge power.
at_max/at_min guards removed — case I handles the safety function.

Return: Zone 1 → timer toggle + mode '1'. Zone 2 → timer toggle + output 0 W + mode '0'. Integral = 0.

SOC protection (Zone 3) remains fully active.

Due to the Solakon ONE hardware ramp (~25 s from min to max), keep the P-factor low. The I-part stays at 0 — at this sluggishness it has no effect.

Priority: AC charging does not start if surplus feed-in (Zone 0) is active. AC charging and tariff charging mutually block each other via the mode guard (mode ≠ '3').

Multi-instance: the error share in the AC-charge PI is its own pool, independent of the zero-feed-in distribution ("Distribution" tab). If multiple instances charge at the same time, they split the same grid surplus via this pool — an instance in mode '1' does not affect it. Output base for the control action: (Σ commanded power of all instances currently charging) × own error share, not this instance's own last commanded value — realigns the split to the weighting on every control action.

tariff.summary: Tariff Arbitrage (Tibber, aWATTar …) — three price tiers
tariff.text:
Cheap (price < cheap threshold): tariff charging starts — fixed charge power until SOC target. No PI controller.
Medium (cheap ≤ price < expensive threshold): discharge-lock — Zone 1 and Zone 2 blocked (output 0 W, mode disabled). Once the price exceeds the expensive threshold, operation is automatically restored.
Expensive (price ≥ expensive threshold): normal SOC logic, no restriction.

Tariff charging and AC charging are independent modules that mutually block each other via the mode guard.

Priority: tariff charging, discharge-lock and its recovery block are suspended while surplus feed-in (Zone 0) is active.

Requires a price sensor with a numeric value in ct/kWh.

dynoff.summary: Dynamic Offset — automatically calculated from grid volatility
dynoff.text:
Calculates the zero-point offset from the standard deviation of grid power over the configured time window.

Formula: offset = clamp(min + max(0, (StdDev − noise) × factor), min, max)

Example (min=30, noise=15, factor=1.5):
• StdDev 5 W → 30 W (minimum)
• StdDev 30 W → 52 W
• StdDev 80 W → 128 W
• StdDev 160 W → 248 W
• StdDev 250 W+ → 250 W (maximum)

Each zone (Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone AC) can be enabled individually and overrides the static offset of that zone.

The StdDev sensor is calculated internally — no external statistics sensor required.

Multiple instances on the same grid sensor: one instance (the group leader) maintains the StdDev ring buffer, all others adopt its value — prevents independent, slightly phase-shifted StdDev calculations per instance.

Trimming (stddev_trim_count): excludes the N highest AND the N lowest individual readings in the window before the calculation — per side, not in total (N=5 → 10 samples excluded). Expressed as a sample count, not a percentage, since the number of samples in the window depends on the grid sensor's update rate. Separates short, rare load spikes (e.g. a compressor or pump inrush lasting a few seconds) from genuine sustained volatility: a spike that fills only a minority of the window's samples falls out entirely; a fluctuation affecting most of the window survives trimming unchanged and still moves the offset. Default 0 = no trimming. Effect directly comparable via the second StdDev value (raw, untrimmed) in the status display.

night.summary: Night Shutdown — disable Zone 2 when PV < PV reserve
night.text:
Affects Zone 2 only (case F): output 0 W, timer toggle, mode → disabled, integral reset.
Zone 1 and AC charging continue running at night.

Threshold: PV reserve from zone settings — no separate parameter.

Reactivation: once PV rises above the PV reserve again, case E applies (integral reset, timer toggle, mode → '1') — provided no tariff lock is active.

debug.summary: Debug — manual intervention in the control state
debug.text:
Reset integral: sets the I-part of the PI controller to 0.

Set zone manually: toggles the internal cycle_active flag and resets the integral.
• Activate Zone 1: cycle_active = true → aggressive discharge, full discharge current.
• Activate Zone 2: cycle_active = false → battery-friendly operation, 0 A discharge current, dynamic output limit.

All actions are logged under 'Last action' in the Status tab.

entities.summary: Entities — every optional sensor assignment for this instance in one place
entities.text:
Bundles the entity-picker fields that would otherwise be scattered across the Zones, Surplus and Tariff tabs. Enable flags and numeric thresholds stay in their respective feature tab — this tab only assigns WHAT is read.

With multiple instances there's also a global default per sensor in the Distribution tab: local (here) overrides global, otherwise the global value applies. If a field is left empty both here and globally, that function has no effect — even if its enable flag is set.

col_descs.entities_all: Optional entity assignments for this instance. Enable flags and numeric thresholds stay in their respective feature tab (Zones, Surplus, Tariff) — this only assigns which entity is read. With multiple instances: local (here) overrides the global value from the Distribution tab, otherwise the global value applies.

p_factor.d: Responds immediately to the current deviation (grid − offset). Higher = more aggressive. Too high: output oscillates permanently. Typical after tuning: 0.8–1.5

i_factor.d: Accumulates deviations over time, eliminates steady-state error. Starting value: 0 — only increase once P-control is stable. Typical: 0.03–0.08

tolerance.d: Deviations within this range do not trigger a PI action. Instead the integral decay kicks in (−5 %/cycle when |integral| > 10).

wait_time.d: Compensates hardware ramp + sensor polling latency after an output change. Without self-adjust: fixed pause. With self-adjust: maximum timeout as safety net.

self_adjust_enabled.d: After each output change, waits for the actual inverter output power. Once actual_power reaches the target ±tolerance, the controller continues. The wait time acts as a maximum timeout.

self_adjust_tolerance.d: Deviation between actual_power and target in watts at which the target is considered reached and the wait ends. Typical: 2–5 W.

zone1_limit.d: SOC exceeds this value → Zone 1 starts. Zone 1 runs through until SOC ≤ Zone 3 threshold — no yo-yo effect. Also active at night.

zone3_limit.d: SOC drops below this value → Zone 3 (safety stop): output 0 W, mode disabled. Must be less than Zone 1 threshold. AC charging remains possible despite Zone 3.

pv_reserve.d: Zone-2 output limit: min(Hard Limit Z1, max(0, PV − reserve)) — PV-based limit capped by Hard Limit Z1. Also the threshold for night shutdown: Zone 2 disabled when PV < reserve.

hard_limit_z0.d: Output power ceiling in Zone 0 (surplus feed-in). The inverter is set to this value while surplus is active. Typically the legal maximum (e.g. 800 W). If the optional export-limit entity is configured, max(Z0, Z1) is written to it on every cycle.

hard_limit_z1.d: Output power ceiling in Zone 1 (discharge) and Zone 2 (PV tracking). In Zone 2 the combined limit min(hard limit Z1, max(0, PV − reserve)) applies. If PV drops suddenly, the PI controller keeps running and corrects output downward.

discharge_max.d: Discharge current in Zone 1. Zone 2 and AC charging automatically set 0 A. Surplus sets 2 A.

offset_1.d: Control target in Zone 1. Positive = controller maintains slight grid import as safety buffer. Negative = controller slightly exports. Overridden when dynamic offset for Zone 1 is active.

offset_2.d: Control target in Zone 2. Recommended: slightly larger than Zone-1 offset (stronger import buffer when battery is discharged conservatively). Overridden when dynamic offset for Zone 2 is active.

surplus_enabled.d: Highest priority — blocks tariff charging, discharge-lock and AC charging while Zone 0 is active. Normal: SOC ≥ threshold + PV surplus. With forecast: PV > Hard Limit Z0 is sufficient (no export threshold, SOC only needs to be above zone 3); exit is blocked while forecast ≥ threshold AND PV > Hard Limit Z0 AND SOC > zone 3 — once one condition drops away, the normal SOC/consumption logic applies.

surplus_soc_threshold.d: Zone 0 only starts at this SOC. Must be above the zone-1 threshold — otherwise regulation pauses with an error message. Recommendation: ~5 % below the app charge limit (e.g. 95 % with max 100 %) — entry is only measurable while the battery is still charging; at the full-charge point the hardware throttles PV down to consumption and the surplus becomes invisible.

surplus_soc_hyst.d: Exit only when SOC < (threshold − hysteresis). Prevents flickering near the threshold. Typical: 3–5 %.

surplus_pv_hyst.d: Entry: PV > output + grid + hysteresis. Exit: PV ≤ output + grid − hysteresis. In multi-instance setups the hysteresis is scaled by the error share — the dead band stays proportional to the consumption reference.

surplus_forecast_enabled.d: When forecast ≥ threshold: surplus starts as soon as PV > Hard Limit Z0 AND SOC > zone-3 threshold (no export threshold required). Forcing stays active while forecast ≥ threshold AND PV > Hard Limit Z0 AND SOC > zone 3 — feeds in early on a big PV day instead of curtailing, without waiting for a full battery. Once PV drops below Hard Limit Z0 (incl. at night: PV = 0), the forecast drops below the threshold or the SOC drops below zone 3, forcing ends and the normal exit (SOC OR consumption) applies — no nightly stick.

surplus_forecast_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "PV Forecast Today" entity (Entities tab) this function stays inactive — shared field with the tariff PV forecast.

surplus_forecast_threshold.d: PV > Hard Limit Z0 + forecast ≥ threshold + SOC > zone-3 threshold → surplus starts without export threshold and stays active while all three conditions hold.

surplus_lock_enabled.d: Keeps Zone 0 alive through short PV dips (clouds): while the power forecast is ≥ lock factor × Hard Limit Z0, the PV exit is blocked — the measured dip must be transient. The SOC exit always stays active, Zone 3 ends surplus at any time. Background: exiting with a full battery enters a state where the hardware throttles PV down to consumption — the surplus becomes unmeasurable and re-entry is delayed by minutes. Risk: if the sensor reports a stuck, too-high value, Zone 0 stays active for just as long — until the SOC exit kicks in.

surplus_lock_sensor.d: Sensor with the currently forecast PV power in W (e.g. Solcast power_now, k-units normalized ×1000 automatically). Feeds the exit lock for Zone 0 (Surplus tab).

surplus_lock_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "Power Forecast Sensor" entity (Entities tab) this lock stays inactive.

surplus_lock_factor.d: Lock active while forecast ≥ factor × Hard Limit Z0. Higher factor = more safety margin against forecast errors. Default: 1.5.

ac_enabled.d: Entry (case G): SOC < target AND no surplus active AND no AC/tariff charge AND mode ≠ '3' AND (grid + Σoutput_discharging) < −hysteresis — sum over all instances in discharge mode, single-instance = own output. Abort (case H): mode = '3' AND ac_charge_active AND no tariff charge AND (SOC ≥ target OR (grid ≥ offset + hysteresis AND own output ≤ 0 W)). SOC protection (Zone 3) remains fully active. Does not start when surplus feed-in (Zone 0) or tariff charging is active.

ac_soc_target.d: Charging stops when SOC reaches this value. Recommended: > Zone-1 threshold — so Zone 1 takes over directly after charging and runs zero-export.

ac_power_limit.d: Absolute ceiling for AC charge power. Passed as max_power to the PI controller.

ac_hysteresis.d: Entry: (grid + Σoutput_discharging) < −hysteresis — sum over all instances in discharge mode. Exit: grid ≥ (offset + hysteresis) AND own output ≤ 0 W. The output ≤ 0 W guard prevents false triggering while the PI is still controlling; `≤` instead of exact `= 0` is more robust against Modbus noise.

ac_offset.d: Control target for grid power in AC charge mode. Negative = export targeted → PI increases charge power. Overridden when dynamic offset for Zone AC is active.

ac_p_factor.d: Proportional gain in AC charge mode. Due to the Solakon ONE hardware ramp (~25 s from min to max), keep low (~0.3–0.5). Starting value: 0.3.

ac_i_factor.d: Integral gain in AC charge mode. Leave at 0 — due to the Solakon ONE hardware ramp (~25 s), the control loop is too sluggish for the I-part to have any effect. P alone is sufficient.

tariff_enabled.d: Cheap (< cheap threshold): tariff charging. Medium (in between): discharge-lock — Zone 1 and Zone 2 blocked. Expensive (≥ expensive threshold): normal SOC logic. Blocked while surplus feed-in (Zone 0) is active. Independent of the AC charging module.

tariff_price_sensor.d: Sensor entity with the current electricity price in ct/kWh. Feeds tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab).

tariff_price_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "Price Sensor" entity (Entities tab) tariff arbitrage stays inactive.

tariff_cheap_threshold.d: Tariff charging starts when price is below this threshold AND SOC < target. Also the lower bound of the discharge-lock.

tariff_cheap_entity.d: Optional input_number entity, overrides the static cheap threshold. Feeds tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab).

tariff_exp_threshold.d: Above this threshold: normal SOC logic, discharge-lock lifts. In between (cheap ≤ price < expensive): discharge-lock Zone 1 and Zone 2. Must be greater than the cheap threshold.

tariff_exp_entity.d: Optional input_number entity, overrides the static expensive threshold. Feeds tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab).

tariff_dynamic_entities_note.d: 🔌 Optional "Dynamic Cheap Threshold" / "Dynamic Expensive Threshold" entities (Entities tab) override the numeric values above when set.

tariff_soc_target.d: Tariff charging stops when this SOC is reached. Independent of the AC charging module's SOC target.

tariff_power.d: Fixed charge power during tariff charging — no PI controller, no dynamic adjustment.

pv_forecast_enabled.d: When active and the forecast sensor reports a value ≥ threshold, tariff charging and discharge-lock are suppressed. Automatic flexibility for sunny days.

pv_forecast_sensor.d: input_number or sensor entity with the expected kWh yield today (e.g. weather integration or Solcast account; Wh/MWh normalized to kWh automatically). Feeds tariff-lock suppression (Tariff tab), Surplus Forecast Override (Surplus tab) and, between 0–12h, Zone-1 Night Forcing (Zones tab).

pv_forecast_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "PV Forecast Today" entity (Entities tab) this function stays inactive.

pv_forecast_threshold.d: When forecast ≥ this value: tariff charging and discharge-lock are blocked, normal zero-export continues.

zone1_force_enabled.d: Allows the Zone-1 discharge cycle to start even below the normal Zone-1 threshold when the target day's PV forecast will refill the battery anyway — prevents charge left unused overnight after a cloudy day. Only the entry is brought forward; the exit still runs through the normal Zone-3 threshold. Only applies while it is currently dark (PV < PV reserve) and SOC is above its own minimum SOC floor (below).

zone1_force_sensor.d: input_number or sensor entity with the expected kWh yield for tomorrow (Wh/MWh normalized to kWh automatically). Feeds Zone-1 Night Forcing (Zones tab), read before midnight — after midnight "PV Forecast Today" above is used automatically instead (same target day, only the sensor changes).

zone1_force_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "PV Forecast Tomorrow" entity (Entities tab) this function stays inactive.

zone1_force_threshold.d: Forcing only applies once the PV forecast for the target day reaches or exceeds this value.

zone1_force_min_soc.d: Dedicated safety floor for Night Forcing, independent of the Zone-3 threshold (which only governs the regular exit). Must lie strictly between the Zone-3 and Zone-1 thresholds — prevents forcing at SOC values where the state-of-charge estimate becomes unreliable.

stddev_window.d: Time window for the standard deviation calculation. Applies to all zones.

stddev_trim_count.d: Number of the highest AND number of the lowest individual readings in the StdDev window that get excluded per side before the calculation — e.g. a value of 5 excludes 10 samples in total (5 lowest + 5 highest), not 5. Expressed as a sample count, not a percentage, since the number of samples in the window varies with the grid sensor's update rate. Separates short, rare load spikes (e.g. a compressor or pump inrush lasting a few seconds) from genuine sustained volatility: a spike that fills only a minority of the window's samples falls entirely into the excluded range; a fluctuation affecting most of the window survives trimming unchanged and still moves the offset. 0 = no trimming (default, previous behavior). Effect visible live via "StdDev (raw)" below.

dyn_z1_enabled.d: Calculates the offset dynamically from the grid StdDev instead of the static value. Overrides the static Zone-1 offset.

dyn_z1_min.d: Base buffer with a calm grid (StdDev ≤ noise threshold). Offset never falls below this value.

dyn_z1_max.d: Upper ceiling of the offset. Offset never exceeds this value, even at very high StdDev.

dyn_z1_noise.d: StdDev below this threshold is treated as measurement noise and does not trigger an offset increase.

dyn_z1_factor.d: Gain above the noise threshold. Formula: buffer = (StdDev − noise) × factor.

dyn_z1_negative.d: Negates the calculated offset (× −1). The control target then lies below 0 W.

dyn_z2_enabled.d: Calculates the offset dynamically from the grid StdDev instead of the static value. Overrides the static Zone-2 offset.

dyn_z2_min.d: Base buffer with a calm grid (StdDev ≤ noise threshold). Offset never falls below this value.

dyn_z2_max.d: Upper ceiling of the offset. Offset never exceeds this value, even at very high StdDev.

dyn_z2_noise.d: StdDev below this threshold is treated as measurement noise and does not trigger an offset increase.

dyn_z2_factor.d: Gain above the noise threshold. Formula: buffer = (StdDev − noise) × factor.

dyn_z2_negative.d: Negates the calculated offset (× −1). The control target then lies below 0 W.

dyn_ac_enabled.d: Calculates the AC charge offset dynamically from the grid StdDev instead of the static value. Overrides the static AC offset.

dyn_ac_min.d: Base buffer with a calm grid (StdDev ≤ noise threshold). Offset never falls below this value.

dyn_ac_max.d: Upper ceiling of the offset. Offset never exceeds this value, even at very high StdDev.

dyn_ac_noise.d: StdDev below this threshold is treated as measurement noise and does not trigger an offset increase.

dyn_ac_factor.d: Gain above the noise threshold. Formula: buffer = (StdDev − noise) × factor.

dyn_ac_negative.d: Negates the calculated offset (× −1). The control target then lies below 0 W.

night_enabled.d: Disable Zone 2 when PV < PV reserve. Zone 1 and AC charging continue running. Zone 2 is not reactivated while a tariff lock (medium/cheap price) is active.

periodic_enabled.d: Runs the regulation loop at a fixed interval — even without sensor changes. Useful for stable households where grid power rarely fluctuates.

periodic_interval.d: Seconds between periodic regulation runs. Minimum: 5 s.

top_card.title: ⚡ Solakon ONE Zero Export
top_card.p1: The Solakon ONE Zero Export integration automatically controls the inverter output power so that grid import is kept as close to 0 W as possible — without exporting to the public grid.
top_card.p2: At its core is a PI controller with grid power as the controlled variable and inverter output power as the manipulated variable. Behaviour is governed by four SOC zones: Zone 1 discharges aggressively, Zone 2 conservatively, Zone 3 blocks discharge, Zone 0 actively exports surplus.
top_card.p3: Optional modules: ☀️ Surplus, ⚡ AC Charging, 💹 Tariff Arbitrage, 📈 Dynamic Offset (per zone individually), 🌙 Night Shutdown. All parameters are stored persistently here in the panel — no YAML, no helper entities.
top_card.prio_heading: Priority and mutual blocking of optional modules:
top_card.prio_note: AC charging and tariff charging mutually block each other via the mode guard (mode ≠ '3'). Surplus feed-in has absolute priority — no other optional module can start while Zone 0 is active.

debug.pi_desc: Manually resets the I-part of the PI controller to 0. Useful after a manual intervention.
debug.zone_desc: Manually switches the discharge cycle and resets the integral.

dist.single_instance_note: Power distribution is only needed with multiple instances.
dist.groups_note: Instances are grouped automatically by their configured grid power sensor — each grid group (e.g. multiple smart meters for separate circuits) gets its own, independent power distribution. With only one group this grouping is invisible, there's just a single shared pool.
dist.global_max_desc: Absolute ceiling for all instances combined — split according to weights. If an instance is capped by its own hard limit (Zones tab), the unused remainder is automatically passed on to instances with headroom (water-filling) — otherwise the pool would never reach this value with unevenly sized instances. Default: 800 W (legal feed-in maximum).
dist.cap_sensor_desc: Battery capacity sensor (in kWh) per instance — used to weight the power split in "Capacity-weighted" mode. The dot next to the field shows entity validity live: green = provides a value, amber = exists but unknown/unavailable, red = does not exist (check for typos):
dist.mode_desc:
Equal → each active instance (mode '1', zero feed-in) receives the same share
SOC-weighted → instance with more usable energy (SOC above minimum) gets more power, regardless of battery size — SOC values equalise over time
Capacity-weighted → like SOC-weighted, additionally × battery capacity (kWh) — useful with differently sized batteries, so the SOC of all instances drops at the same rate. Requires a valid capacity sensor per instance below.
SOC-switching → only one instance discharges at a time, exclusively (100 %), the others sit idle. Hands over to the instance with the highest remaining SOC once the active one has dropped by the divergence threshold — instances are worked through one after another instead of drawing on all of them in parallel.

AC charging has its own, independent distribution pool (see the "AC Charging" tab).

If, under SOC-weighted/Capacity-weighted/SOC-switching, another instance's SOC or capacity sensor is currently unavailable, the pool falls back to equal distribution for that cycle — shown as a message in the status/error field, never a silent fallback.
dist.soc_switch_divergence_desc: The active instance discharges exclusively until its SOC has dropped by this value since taking over — then the instance with the highest remaining SOC takes over. Smaller values = more frequent switching, finer equalisation; larger values = less frequent switching, each instance discharges further down in one go. If the active instance was briefly in Zone 0 (surplus feed-in), the threshold is re-anchored to the current SOC once it leaves Zone 0 — so that period doesn't count twice against the budget.
dist.global_sensors_desc: Cross-instance default for sensors that typically apply to the whole household (one weather/Solcast account, one electricity tariff) — each instance can optionally override locally in its own tab, otherwise this value applies. The dot next to each field shows entity validity live (green/amber/red).
dist.global_pv_today_desc: Feeds the Surplus Forecast Override (Zone-0 tab), the Tariff Lock suppression (Tariff tab) and, between 0–12h, Zone-1 Night Forcing (Zones tab), unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_pv_tomorrow_desc: Feeds the Zone-1 Night Forcing (Zones tab). Read before midnight; after midnight "PV Forecast Today" above is used automatically instead (same target day).
dist.global_surplus_lock_desc: Feeds the Zone-0 exit lock (Zone-0 tab), unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_tariff_price_desc: Feeds the tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab), unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_tariff_cheap_desc: Optional input_number entity, overrides the static cheap threshold, unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_tariff_exp_desc: Optional input_number entity, overrides the static expensive threshold, unless an instance overrides it locally.
